summary: A Voice for the Abandoned is a 5–7 minute animated educational video for students aged 6 to 14 that explores the forgotten landers, rovers, and equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Because most school age kids only learn about active missions, our video bridges that gap using simple, everyday language and minimalistic visuals so learners with zero prior space knowledge can follow along. By highlighting iconic missions like Apollo 11, Surveyor 3, Lunokhod 1, and Opportunity, the project reframes "space junk" as preserved time capsules and active scientific instruments made to inspire lasting curiosity and act as an easy-to-share starting point for future learning episodes
details: A Voice for the Abandoned is a 5–7 minute faceless educational animated video designed for students aged 6 to 14. Most space media focuses exclusively on active missions, leaving the retired rovers, landers, and descent stages sitting silently on the Moon and Mars largely forgotten. Our video takes viewers on an engaging guided tour of historic space hardware including: Apollo 11, Surveyor 3, Lunokhod 1, and the Opportunity rover explaining what they were built to do, why they were left behind, and how some of them still contribute to science today!
